prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's fan-out-damped cut lowers total cut but leaves crit_cross unchanged because the cut term treats every pin of a net equally; adding a pin-level criticality weight inside the expected-cut product (each pin's log-prob scaled by 1 + alpha * normalized crit rank of that pin) will pull critical pins of the same net together, lowering crit-pair cross-tier and thus TNS.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.151 robust(mean-std)=-0.116 min_case=-0.143 seed_std=0.091 tns_mean=-0.003 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.000 dWNS=+2.3% dTNS=-1.4% per-seed=[-0.03 +0.00 +0.03]
  C2: score=-0.008 dWNS=-6.7% dTNS=+2.9% per-seed=[+0.00 -0.05 +0.02]
  C3: score=-0.143 dWNS=-26.6% dTNS=-2.5% per-seed=[+0.00 +0.02 -0.45]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->142, wcut 421->435, crit_cross 0.011->0.011, repair_flips 103->102, changed-vs-baseline 2.0%
  C2: cut 318->310, wcut 1007->974, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->238, changed-vs-baseline 4.4%
  C3: cut 582->573, wcut 1955->1916, crit_cross 0.069->0.040, repair_flips 353->349, changed-vs-baseline 9.2%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response: (1) Partially: crit_cross fell only on C3 (0.069→0.040) with cut also down (582→573), but total cut worsened overall (total=-0.151) and TNS barely moved (-0.003). (2) C3 drove the effect—lower crit-pair cross-tier and fewer repair flips (353→349); C1/C2 showed no crit_cross change and C1 cut rose (137→142). Mechanism consistent with pin-level weighting pulling critical pins together, but gains don't generalize. (3) Seed spread is high (seed_std=0.091; C3 per-seed -0.45 outlier)—not acceptable. (4) Gate alpha by net criticality density or anneal it, and re-test on C3-like circuits to confirm the crit_cross→TNS link before scaling.
